A gripping mystery that humbled me.

I didn’t expect the story to take such a dark and mysterious turn. The first two chapters were smooth sailing—easy enough that I felt pretty confident in my detective skills. But once the logic started getting really complicated, I realized my brain just couldn't keep up anymore.

Even so, this is a great game. The voice acting is solid, the music fits the mood perfectly, and you really can't fault the classic pixel art style. It has so much charm.

Honestly, I have so much respect for anyone who managed to solve everything from start to finish without a single guide. As for me, I’ll be admiring the story from the sidelines while looking up the answers. 😂

Puede ser que algunas veces te quedes estancadx pero nada que un rato pensando y recordando bien que podes combinar, ver, escuchar y a donde no ir lo resuelva. La historia era sumamente atractiva, los personajes tienen todos una personalidad que hace que se les note el laburo detrás. Toda pizca de información nueva hace que te quedes esperando más.
Y, finalmente, el capitulo 4 y 5. No tengo palabras, acabo de terminar el juego a las 3:58am y me inspiró tanto que me ♥♥♥♥ a escribir esta reseña. El capitulo 4, sin decir nada que pueda llevar a spoiler, tiene ya tanta profundidad que no podes dejar de jugar. Comienza a haber más emociones relacionadas con la familia de Kathy, nos encontramos varias veces al borde del llanto y, por supuesto, nada de lo que creímos hasta un capitulo anterior es como lo pensamos.
El capitulo 5 es una maravilla, no diré más porque terminaría, de alguna manera, spoileando.
En fin, 100% recomendado a los fans y también no fans de los point and click.

Wcielamy się w tytułową Kathy Rain - studentkę dziennikarstwa, której właśnie zmarł nie widziany od 15 lat dziadek. Chcąc nie chcąc Kathy wyrusza swoim motocyklem na pogrzeb. To właśnie wokół osoby zmarłego dziadka kręci się główna intryga. Bohaterka stara się odkryć co się z nim stało 14 lat wcześniej kiedy to został znaleziony przez policję w lesie i od tamtego czasu nie wrócił do pełni sił tak fizycznych, jak i umysłowych. Opowieść jest poprowadzona całkiem sprawnie, Kathy niczym początkujący detektyw stara się iść po nitce do kłębka. Fabuła, podobnie jak w ogrywanym ostatnio przeze mnie Sherlocku Holmesie: The Silver Earring, podzielona jest na pięć dni. Z każdym kolejnym dniem pojawiają się nowe tropy i wskazówki. Poznajemy również coraz lepiej przeszłość bohaterki, która nie była usłana różami. Stąd ten jej buntowniczy wizerunek i charakter. Kathy nie rusza się nigdzie bez paczki fajek, zapalniczki i paralizatora. Odkrywanie tajemnic zmarłego dziadka jest więc dla niej swego rodzaju terapią w trakcie której będzie musiała zajrzeć w głąb siebie. Końcówka w stylu Lyncha nie popsuła mi odbioru historii. Uważam, że zakończenie było całkiem zgrabne.

Zagadki nie są zbyt trudne i grę przechodzi się w miarę płynnie. Z drugiej strony nie jest to gra Telltale i jest kilka momentów przy których trzeba pogłówkować nieco dłużej. Najważniejsze, że generalnie wszystko jest dość logiczne. Nie ma tutaj typowego dla niektórych point&clicków łączenia gumowej kaczuszki ze śrubokrętem by stworzyć helikopter. Czasem trzeba przesłuchać jakąś kasetę na dyktafonie by wyłapać odpowiednie fakty, czasem gdzieś zadzwonić, przeszukać książkę telefoniczną w poszukiwaniu adresu, najczęściej jednak rozmawiamy z poszczególnymi osobami.

Pixel artowa grafika jest przyjemna dla oka, muzyka może nie zapada w pamięć, ale stanowi przyjemne tło. Również do głosów postaci nie można się przyczepić. Lokacje może nie są duże, ale w trakcie przygody odwiedzimy m.in. cmentarz, komisariat policji czy bar gangu motocyklowego. Klimacik lat 90. w wydaniu amerykańskim również robi robotę.

Widzę, że jest wersja reżyserska, która rozszerza grę. Może kiedyś ją zakupię razem z "dwójką", gdy cena nieco spadnie, gdyż obok wspomnianego Sherlocka Holmesa jest to jedna z przyjemniejszych przygodówek w jakie grałem ostatnimi czasy.

I loved 90s point and click adventure games growing up, so I gave this a try. The atmosphere and art is nice, but three things turned me off. (1) The 90s nostalgia feels incomplete. Cathy doesn't look or sound like someone from the 90s (at least to me, who grew up in the 90s). She feels like a contemporary insert. (2) There was nothing that made me interested in playing as Cathy specifically and hearing her view point for the whole game, and that's largely because (3) She's a mean, unempathetic character. The example that really turned me off: Her grandmother, who just buried a loved one, invites her to chat and asks Kathy to tell her about her life. Kathy says, "Well, I ride a motorcycle, in case you missed it outside..." with this sarcastic lilt of "...you know, if you're an idiot." That's such an unnecessarily mean thing to say to your grieving grandmother who just invited you into her home after years of not talking, no hesitation or questions asked. Kathy talks like a un-socialized 15 yr old instead of a 20 year old journalism major.  Her wise-cracking sarcasm doesn't feel on point or badass, or even charmingly misguided. It feels abusive and solipsistic. 

If her sarcasm doesn't bother you, you might like this game. But as someone who's been on the receiving end of this "I'm lashing out with condescending snark to cover up my own hurt" bullying a good deal when I was a teenager (in the 90s), it really turns me off to the character. I think I'd rather play a game as her earnest roommate, who despite her seeming un-coolness, makes for an actually pretty badass detective with her organized notes and color printer.

Kathy Rain is a narrative-focused adventure that blends classic point-and-click design with a deeply personal mystery, resulting in an experience that feels both nostalgic and emotionally grounded. Set in the mid-1990s, the game follows Kathy Rain, a sharp-tongued journalism student who returns to her hometown after the death of her grandfather. What begins as a seemingly straightforward investigation into his passing slowly unfolds into a layered story about family trauma, small-town secrets, and the lasting scars left by unresolved events. From the opening moments, the game establishes a strong sense of place and character, drawing players into a world that feels lived-in and quietly troubled.

Kathy herself is one of the game’s greatest strengths. She is portrayed as intelligent, stubborn, and emotionally guarded, shaped by a difficult upbringing and strained family relationships. Her dialogue is often sarcastic and blunt, but beneath that exterior lies a character driven by curiosity and unresolved grief. This makes her investigation feel personal rather than procedural, as each discovery connects not just to the mystery at hand but also to her own identity and past. The writing does an excellent job of letting her personality shine through natural conversations rather than heavy exposition, making her feel like a fully realized protagonist rather than a genre archetype.

The gameplay adheres closely to traditional point-and-click mechanics, emphasizing exploration, dialogue, and inventory-based puzzles. Players move between locations, talk to locals, gather clues, and gradually piece together information through careful observation. The puzzles are generally logical and grounded in the narrative, avoiding excessive obscurity and encouraging players to think contextually about the world and its characters. While there are moments of increased difficulty, these tend to arise from narrative complexity rather than arbitrary design, keeping frustration to a minimum and maintaining immersion.

Narratively, Kathy Rain excels at building tension through gradual revelation. As Kathy digs deeper into her grandfather’s history, the story widens to encompass other residents of Conwell Springs, each with their own memories and secrets. The pacing allows the mystery to breathe, layering personal drama, investigative intrigue, and unsettling implications without rushing to conclusions. The game takes a bold turn into darker and more surreal territory as it progresses, a choice that may surprise some players but ultimately reinforces the story’s themes of obsession, repression, and the cost of uncovering hidden truths.

Visually, the game embraces a detailed pixel art style that pays homage to classic adventure games while still feeling contemporary. The environments are richly atmospheric, using lighting, color, and composition to convey mood rather than realism. Conwell Springs feels isolated and slightly decayed, reinforcing the sense that the town is holding onto secrets it would rather forget. The soundtrack complements this perfectly, combining moody ambient tracks with melodic themes that underscore both quiet reflection and moments of tension.

The Director’s Cut version further enhances the experience by refining visuals, expanding locations, and adding full voice acting. These additions strengthen character interactions and make emotional beats land more effectively, without altering the core structure that made the original release compelling. The voice performances, in particular, add nuance to conversations and help distinguish the personalities of the supporting cast, making the town feel more alive and believable.

Overall, Kathy Rain is a thoughtfully crafted adventure that stands out through its strong protagonist, grounded mystery, and confident storytelling. It respects the traditions of classic point-and-click games while updating them with modern pacing and emotional depth. Though its length is relatively modest, the experience feels complete and purposeful, leaving a lasting impression through its characters and themes rather than sheer scale. For players who appreciate narrative-driven games with a focus on character and atmosphere, Kathy Rain remains a standout example of how powerful a well-told mystery can be.

[b]Kathy Rain[/b] ist ein klassisches [b]Point-&-Click[/b] von [b]Clifftop Games[/b] aus 2016. 
Wir spielen die junge US-amerikanische Journalistik-Studentin "Kathy Rain", die durch ihre Mitbewohnerin vom Tod ihres Großvaters erfährt, sich darauf hin nach langer Zeit mit der Geschichte des Verstorbenen und ihrer restlichen Familie beschäftigt. 
Die [b]Grafik[/b] der Figuren ist sehr pixel-stylish, vor allem die handgezeichneten Hintergründe fand ich [u]wunderbar[/u] arrangiert. 
Die Sprachausgabe gibt es nur in [b]Englisch[/b], alles andere (Menü, UI, Untertitel etc.) sind in [b]Deutsch[/b] vorhanden. 

Das Spiel dauert rund 6,5 bis 8 Stunden. Wer es mit allen 20 Achievements vervollständigen möchte, sollte es (ggf. mit Zuhilfenahme von Guides) in der gleichen Zeit locker hinbekommen. 

[b][u]Fazit[/u]:[/b] 
Ich empfehle dieses nette [b]Point-&-Click-Abenteuer[/b] allen Fans des Genres ohne Bedenken. 
Ich finde den [b]regulären Vollpreis[/b] des Spiels [u]fair und angemessen[/u], wer Zweifel hat, sollte es sich zumindest auf die [b]eigene Wunschliste[/b] setzen, um benachrichtigt zu werden, wenn es mal wieder im [b]Steam-Sale[/b] landet.

Leider nicht ganz happy als "Point & Click".
Vom Trailer und den Screenshots hatte ich ein wenig das Gefühl der alten guten Point & Click bekommen, die ich sehr gerne gespielt habe (Day of the Tentacle, Sam & Max, Monkey Island und Konsorten).
Das Spiel ist aber leider nicht so und eher eine kleine (und sehr kurze) "interaktive" Story, die etwas merkwürdig ist.

Zudem habe ich den Fehler gemacht und zuerst den Director's Cut gespielt, die in vielerlei Hinsicht einfach besser ist (vor allem Steuerung, manche Übersetzung, etc.).

Hauptcharakter ist auch ziemlich fragwürdig und legt ein komisches Verhalten an den Tag. Die Story dreht ziemlich merkwürdig in eine Art "Anti-Religion" ab.
Sehr linear, dafür schicker Artstyle und gute englische Vertonung. Deutsche Textübersetzung ist gut und verständlich, allerdings im Director's Cut nochmal verbessert.

Preislich finde ich es fast etwas zu hoch angesetzt für den erhaltenen Inhalt.
Wenn man es dennoch spielen möchte, rate ich eher zum Director's Cut und wenn es mal heruntergesetzt ist.

It is only by chance that the young student Kathy Rain finds out that her grandfather, which she never really got to know, passed away. As she starts to investigate his death she comes across many mysteries and more questions than she expected to find. 

Kathy Rains is a very neat and well presented point & click adventure that shines with all the aspects a game in this genre should have, at least in my opinion: 

- Deep atmosphere that is somehow cozy and thrilling at the same time
- Interesting and likeable protagonist (Kathy is finally not an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ character even though she is not afraid to speak her mind)
- beautiful voice acting throughout the whole game!
- idyllic music and beautiful pixel graphics
- great puzzles which are solvable 

The story takes place in the 90s, right before mobile phones were invented and feels quite nostalgic, yet still surprised me with very fresh dialogues and a protagonist who wasn't scared to knock down somebody who comes in her way. The  investigative plot feels enthralling and personal. The looks of the old version (which I played) are still very good and I had almost no problems or bugs (one time the game crashed on my while I was doing something in the background of my pc). The gameplay is very intuitive and all puzzles  are comprehensible, logical and doable... except for the one in the church, but that's what walkthroughs are there for, aren't they?

The only thing I maybe maaaybe would complain about is the rushed ending, which came to me a bit by surprise - but it fitted the story, so I can't really complain a lot. Grab it (especially when its on sale)!
